Chicago White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery achieved MLB history, but not in a good way.

During Thursday's game against the Kansas City Royals, Montgomery struck out in his second at-bat, tying Mark Reynolds' single-season MLB record of 223 strikeouts.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV on White Sox return to postseason: 'Great things happen in Chicago'
articles.summary: The White Sox have not won a playoff since series claiming the 2005 World Series title.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox are back in the playoffs after clinching a spot on Thursday with a 9-1 win over the Kansas City Royals . The postseason appearance ends a five-year drought for the franchise, which had three-straight 100-loss seasons entering the 2026 campaign.

There were a number of factors that went into the successful regular season such as the offensive production from Miguel Vargas , Colson Montgomery and offseason addition Munetaka Murakami , as well as the pitching staff led by Sean Burke .

Another potential factor is the power of long-time White Sox fan Robert Prevost, better known now as Pope Leo XIV.

The Holy Father's fandom has been heavily documented, as he was in attendance at the 2005 World Series , which the White Sox won.

So would Pope Leo's new status have anything to do with the turnaround season for his favorite baseball team?

"No comment," Leo said , smiling when asked on the papal plane. "Great things happen in Chicago ."

The team and the fanbase have embraced their famous fan since he became Pope. As the playoffs get set to begin next week, everyone on the South Side of Chicago is hoping Leo's good luck will lead to a championship parade at the end of October.

articles.title: Red Sox vs. Yankees Set for 2026 MLB Playoffs Bracket, Updated Standings Ahead of Postseason
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees will renew their rivalry in the Wild Card round of the 2026 MLB playoffs.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees will renew their rivalry in the Wild Card round of the 2026 MLB playoffs.

The Red Sox locked in the matchup Thursday with a 4-3 win over the visiting Chicago Cubs.

The Red Sox are now set to travel to the Bronx for Game 1 of the Wild Card series next Tuesday.

The teams will return Wednesday for Game 2 and, if necessary, could finish out the series Thursday with a winner-takes-all Game 3. All three games will be broadcast on NBC/NBCSN and stream on Peacock.

This marks the seventh time the Red Sox and Yankees have met one another in the postseason, with the most recent matchup taking place during the 2025 Wild Card series.

The Yankees lost the opening game of that series before coming back to win Game 2.

Then-Yankees pitcher Garrett Crochet helped his club close out the Game 3 win and become the third team in history to advance to the divisional series after opening the postseason with a Wild Card loss.

The Yankees went 7-6 against the Red Sox (4-2 at home) this season, securing the regular-season series victory with a 16-1 blowout Aug. 30 at Yankee Stadium.

The home team is heading into the matchup with an intimidating pitching rotation led by Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón but potentially missing Aaron Judge, who could miss the Wild Card round with a right calf strain.

The Red Sox have some injury questions of their own with closer Aroldis Chapman and outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela both dealing with recent health issues, but Boston also boasts a strong top-of-the rotation in Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez.

These clubs, which have put together two of the most efficient rotations in MLB this season, could be set for a pitching duel when Game 1 starts this Tuesday at a time yet to be determined.

articles.title: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Apologizes for Remarks on $500M Blue Jays Contract, 'I Regret My Comments'
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. sparked backlash after recent comments regarding the 14-year, $500 million contract extension he signed last offseason, and now the six-time All-Star is profusely apologizing for his remarks as his tough 2026 campaign nears its end.
articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. sparked backlash after recent comments regarding the 14-year, $500 million contract extension he signed last offseason, and now the six-time All-Star is profusely apologizing for his remarks as his tough 2026 campaign nears its end.

Pope Leo jokes about White Sox playoff return

During an interview with Veronica Batista on the program, "Grandes Ligas," Guerrero had this to say (Spanish-to-English translation via ESPN ):

"I want people to understand one thing. The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did," Guerrero told Batista. "They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 [home runs] every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished. People are confused about that, but I think the same way they do. Like, sometimes I even say to myself, 'Bro, they gave you all that money and you're out here doing nothing.' But I try.

"You know how it is with fans, when you're good, they're with you 100%. But when you smell like s---, like we like to say here, nobody supports you. The ones who support you are the ones who stay with you. Those are my real fans and I considered them my family."

Last year, Guerrero nearly helped guide the Blue Jays to their first World Series title since 1993. He hit .292 (.848 OPS) with 23 home runs and 84 RBI before following that up with a scorching-hot postseason (eight home runs, 17 RBI, .397 average, 1.289 OPS).

However, this season has been a nightmare for Guerrero and the last-place Jays. The eight-year veteran's numbers have dipped significantly (nine home runs, 56 RBI, .263 average, .695 OPS).

As John Henry of MLB.com noted, Guerrero has dealt with back and hamstring issues during this season. He also suffered a concussion after a collision with New York Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr.

Naturally, Blue Jays fans may not want to hear that Guerrero was paid for his past accomplishments, considering (a) his performance and (b) the length and money on his upcoming contract years.

Guerrero initially doubled down on his initial remarks.

"No, I don't regret myself. I'm not lying with what I say," Guerrero said via an interpreter, per ESPN. "I understand some fans, they don't understand the way and what I was trying to say specifically, but what I said is the way I feel."

However, Guerrero has since changed his stance.

The 2026 season was a lost one for a Blue Jays squad that saw a host of players regress after a tremendous and magical 2025 campaign.

Next season, should there be one in the face of a potential lockout, brings new hope that this team, led by Guerrero, can meet its ceiling and bounce back.

articles.title: Blue Jays' Vladimir Guerrero Jr. apologizes for comments about $500 million contract and fan support amid subpar season
articles.summary: Guerrero heard from his Hall of Fame father, who told him that his remarks were wrong and he needed to apologize for them.
articles.body:
Vladimir Guerrero Jr . didn't have a good 2026 season for the Toronto Blue Jays .

But to prevent the disappointing season from ending on a bitter note, one which could have lingered into the offseason, the six-time All-Star is apologizing for comments he made to a Spanish-language reporter. In the interview, Guerrero was defensive about the 14-year, $500 million contract extension he signed last year and whether he's fulfilling the expectations that blockbuster deal established.

"The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did," Guerrero said in an interview with Veronica Batista of Noticias Telemicro ( via MLB.com ). "They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished."

Guerrero went on to say "real fans" were the ones that supported him even when he has a subpar performance.

"The fans, I know how they are," he added ( translated by reporter Héctor Gómez ). "When you are doing great, they are 100% behind you, but when you are not at your best, not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."

The Blue Jays first baseman followed up by saying he didn't regret those statements . As could be expected, fans didn't receive those remarks well. That led to him apologizing on Friday.

"I regret my comments the other day," Guerrero Jr. told reporters through an interpreter, via SportsNet . "I felt from my heart that my fans and my teammates needed an apology from me. I'm going to continue working hard to make my contract great."

Either Guerrero realized that what he said was poorly received or someone enlightened him. It appears to have been the latter. The eight-year veteran said that his father, Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero, told him that he made a mistake.

"He told me what I did was wrong and to make sure that I do what I'm doing right now — to give my fans an apology," he said, via SportsNet.

Guerrero has only nine home runs going into this weekend's final three-game series with the Cincinnati Reds . But even if he reaches double digits to go with his .263/.335/.360 slash line, that is far below the production expected from a former 40-homer slugger who's being paid an average of $35 million per year.

The Blue Jays followed up last year's World Series appearance with a losing record. Depending on how Toronto plays in its final three games, they will finish in either fourth or fifth place in the American League East. If Guerrero hit up to his standards, perhaps the season would have had a different outcome.

Yet a fresh start next season would have been more difficult if fans held resentment to the Blue Jays' top player. Obviously, hitting 25 to 30 home runs would turn perception around. But apologizing could also help win at least some of those supporters back.

articles.title: Red Sox move final game of series vs. Cubs to Tampa Bay's Tropicana Field to avoid nor'easter
articles.summary: The threat of inclement weather had already forced Boston and Chicago to play a doubleheader on Friday.
articles.body:
A massive nor'easter has led the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs to take drastic measures for their regular-season finale. The league is moving the final game of the series from Fenway Park to the Tampa Bay Rays ' Tropicana Field in order to avoid the storm, which is set to hit the northeastern United States this weekend.

The game, which was originally scheduled for 7:15 p.m. ET Saturday, will instead take place at 3:05 p.m. Sunday in Tampa . The Red Sox announced the move on Friday, shortly before the second game of a doubleheader between the Sox and Cubs. Tickets will be fully refunded, per the team.

Friday's Cubs-Sox doubleheader was also a choice made because of the storm. Earlier this week, the league adjusted the series by moving Sunday's game to Friday as part of a doubleheader . Both teams will travel to Florida after the conclusion of the second game Friday, "to ensure the safety of both traveling parties," per the Sox.

In a statement, Rays CEO Ken Babby said the team is "proud to support" MLB by hosting the game, citing a desire to help "ensure fans can enjoy this matchup despite the weather challenges in the Northeast," via Ryan Bass of MLB.TV .

Babby noted that the Rays are familiar with weather challenges, as the team had to play the entire 2025 season in an alternate venue after Tropicana Field's roof was heavily damaged by Hurricane Milton in 2024.

"When Tropicana Field was damaged, clubs throughout the league stepped up to support our organization during an incredibly challenging time," Babby said, via Bass. "We're grateful for that solidarity and are pleased to return the favor by welcoming the Cubs, Red Sox, and their fans to Tropicana Field on Sunday."

This weekend's nor'easter is set to bring high winds and heavy rain across the northeast, with potential floods expected along the coasts. Multiple advisories have been issued by the National Weather Service , starting Friday and running through Sunday.

Boston is not the only area that is expected to be affected: The storm will hit New York as well, which led the Yankees to adjust their final regular-season series , too. The Yankees, hosting the Baltimore Orioles this weekend, switched to a doubleheader on Friday, with the final game of the series still set to take place in the Bronx on Sunday.

articles.title: Bill Giles Dies at 92, Former Phillies Owner and Executive Helped Create Phanatic Mascot
articles.summary: Former Philadelphia Phillies executive Bill Giles, who led the team to a pair of National League titles during his tenure as president and played an instrumental role in the creation of the legendary Phillie Phanatic, has died at the age of 92.
articles.body:
Former Philadelphia Phillies executive Bill Giles, who led the team to a pair of National League titles during his tenure as president and played an instrumental role in the creation of the legendary Phillie Phanatic, has died at the age of 92.

Giles, a son of former National League president Warren Giles, enjoyed a long and successful career with the Phillies beginning in 1969, when he began serving as a vice president (business operations).

Giles began his rise in the organization three years later thanks to a promotion to executive vice president. Giles then organized a group that bought the Phillies in 1981, and he then served as the team's president and CEO until 1997. He moved into a chairman role before the Phillies named him chairman emeritus in 2015.

Todd Zolecki of MLB.com provided more commentary on Giles' strong and long-lasting impact.

"Giles, once called the P.T. Barnum of baseball because he tried just about anything to get people to the ballpark, joined the Phillies to help them close Connie Mack Stadium and open Veterans Stadium in 1971. He quickly hired the legendary Harry Kalas from Houston to be one of the team's broadcasters. He later helped create the Phillie Phanatic, convinced free agent Pete Rose to come to Philadelphia, and in 1981 led a group that bought the Phillies from the Carpenter family. As team president from 1981-97, he led the Phillies as they won National League pennants in 1983 and '93."

Phillies third baseman (and Baseball Hall of Famer) Mike Schmidt was the team's big star (and one of the biggest stars in baseball) in the 1980s while Schmidt , and he provided a statement after news of Giles' passing.

"Sad news today as we learned of the passing of a dear friend of the Phillies family, Bill Giles," Schmidt said in the statement, per Zolecki.

"Bill was the heart and soul of the organization for over two decades. He was a close personal friend to so many of us. He will always be a big part of Phillies history. Prayers go to the Giles family in this time of mourning."

Numerous people offered their condolences and remembrances upon his passing.

The Phillies held a moment of silence for Giles prior to their home game against the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday evening.

Giles was preceded in death by his wife, Nancy, of 64 years. He is survived by his three sons and eight grandchildren.

articles.title: Mets clinch last place in NL East with MLB's second-highest payroll at $357 million
articles.summary: The second-highest payroll in MLB bought the Mets a last-place finish, their first since 2003.
articles.body:
With their 7-6 loss to the Washington Nationals on Friday, the New York Mets clinched last place in the National League East.

A 73-87 record — which can be 75-87 at best and 73-89 at worst with two games remaining — was not what the Mets, their fans and the media covering them expected from the second-highest player payroll in Major League Baseball.

The Mets carried a $357 million payroll for that last-place finish this season, according to FanGraphs . Presuming they finish with 73 wins, that's nearly $5 million per victory. Compare that to the Los Angeles Dodgers ' MLB-high $408 million and their 97 victories going into Friday night. They're paying $4.2 million per win.

Not since 2003 had the Mets finished last in the NL East. While they weren't nearly as successful as the team and its fans would have liked during the ensuing 23 years, they did advance to three NL Championship Series and play in one World Series. The Mets won 101 games in 2022.

The 2026 season went sour from the start as the Mets went 7-19 in April. Before May 1, they were 11.5 games out of first place in the NL East. One month later, the Mets were 14 games back. From there, they never got closer than within 13 games of the lead. By the end of June, the Mets were 34-47 and manager Carlos Mendoza was fired .

During the second half of the season, the best entertainment for Mets fans may have been reporter Steve Gelbs rating MLB ballpark hot dogs for his "Let's Be Frank" segment on the SNY broadcasts.

Last season, the Mets finished second in the division with an 83-79 mark. With team owner Steve Cohen bankrolling a massive budget and president of baseball operations David Stearns once considered among the brightest executives in MLB, it wasn't unreasonable to assume that first place was attainable.

The bullpen was bolstered with the signings of Devin Williams and Luke Weaver . Bo Bichette , Jorge Polanco , Marcus Semien and Luis Robert Jr. were added to the lineup. Freddy Peralta provided a top-three starter to the rotation.

But other than Weaver, none of those signings paid off. And a middle reliever — even one with an 1.84 ERA before Weaver was dealt to the Pittsburgh Pirates at the trade deadline — isn't likely to be the difference between second place and first.

With two games remaining, Bichette has a .259/.310/.386 slash line. Semien is batting .216 with a .624 OPS. Polanco only played in 37 games due to Achilles, ankle and wrist injuries . Williams has a 4.54 ERA, while Peralta carried a 4.99 ERA before he was traded to the Tampa Bay Rays .

Pete Alonso reminded Mets fans of the team's failings

Meanwhile, the Mets' failings this season and misguided decisions by the front office were embodied by former first baseman Pete Alonso. A fan favorite and face-of-the-franchise type that teams yearn for, Alonso saw the Baltimore Orioles show him love with a five-year, $155 million contract , signed with them and led the AL in RBI.

Alonso provided Mets fans with a bittersweet reminder of his success in Queens by returning late in the season with the Orioles and getting a standing ovation from the Citi Field crowd.

One night later, he hit his 300th career home run in his former home ballpark, drawing such a positive reaction from fans that current Mets players like Sean Manaea expressed disbelief and resentment .

Mets have some bright spots going into 2027

While Stearns will have to do a far better job in evaluating talent and utilizing the exorbitant resources provided to him by Cohen, the Mets have some young talent that makes next season potentially exciting.

Outfielder Carson Benge became the first Mets rookie to hit 20 home runs and steal 20 bases in team history. Nolan McLean is one of the top young starting pitchers in MLB, compiling a 3.16 ERA with 194 strikeouts in 179 2/3 innings.

Despite missing 48 games with two separate calf injuries , Juan Soto still hit 27 home runs with a .274/.393/.522 slash line. AJ Ewing provided excellent defense in center field, according to advanced metrics , with 5 Defensive Runs Saved and 3 Outs Above Average. Left-hander Zac Thornton appears to have a future in the starting rotation with a 3.42 ERA in 15 appearances.

Mets fans said goodbye to radio announcer Howie Rose, who called his final radio broadcast for the team after more than 30 years in the booth. On the TV side, even when the team is playing badly, Mets fans have a winner with SNY broadcasters Gary Cohen, Ron Darling and Keith Hernandez, ranked as one of the best by Awful Announcing readers.

But the best reason for the Mets and their fans to be hopeful might be as simple as next season can't possibly be worse than this one was. Right?

articles.title: The AL Worst: Astros and Rangers both lose, guaranteeing MLB's first division champ without a winning record
articles.summary: An 81-81 AL West champion is currently the best-case scenario.
articles.body:
The American League West, the worst division in baseball, got a little bit worse on Friday. It was enough to officially push the group into unprecedented territory.

The Houston Astros and the Texas Rangers , the two teams atop the division, both lost, pushing their records to 79-81 with two games left to play. That officially guarantees it won't be a winning team uncorking the champagne at some point in the next days.

It will be the first time in MLB history that a team .500 or worse wins a division.

Before 2026, the division champ closest to .500 was the 2005 San Diego Padres , who won the NL West with an 82-80 record then got swept in the NLDS by the St. Louis Cardinals . There have been playoff teams at or below .500 before, but never a division champ.

Whichever team wins the division, it will then get to host a wild-card series against the AL's third wild-card team. The two other wild-card teams, the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox , will play each other despite both of them having a better record than the two teams in the other series.

The Astros own the tiebreaker against the Rangers, so they effectively have the lead going into the weekend. They will continue playing the A's and Twins, respectively, with the Rangers needing to win one more game than the Astros to steal the division.

In total, the AL West is 84 games below .500 with a combined -473 run differential. Every team is in the red in the latter stat, with the Rangers "leading" the pack at -48. There are 13 teams in MLB who would be leading the division if they were in there. That includes the Arizona Diamondbacks and Pittsburgh Pirates , who do not currently have a playoff spot.

This is a division so bad that three of its five teams — the Astros, the Angels and the A's — have fired their general managers this season, a group that includes one of the division leaders.

It's a wide gamut of misery as well. The Mariners are one of the most disappointing teams in baseball after last year's supposed breakthrough . The Astros and Rangers have both won titles in the past five years and fallen off considerably. The A's are currently playing in a minor-league stadium after a messy divorce from Oakland. The Angels haven't had a winning season since the year "Mad Men" went off the air.

It's all tremendously awkward. It will be awkward when a group of men celebrate winning a crown almost by default. It will be awkward when a stadium welcomes a team with a better record for an ill-deserved playoff series. It will be awkward when the other four teams look at themselves and wonder what might have been in a season with the lowest of bars to clear.

articles.title: Key Phillies executive, last National League president, dies at 92
articles.summary: The executive who rose to an ownership position oversaw the Phillies' first World Series championship.
articles.body:
Bill Giles, a longtime Philadelphia Phillies executive and former owner who helped shape the franchise's business operations, fan experience and championship teams, died Friday at his home in Gladwyne, Pennsylvania. He was 92 .

Born in Rochester, N.Y., in 1934, Giles followed in the footsteps of his father, Warren C. Giles, the president and general manager of the Cincinnati Reds (1937-51) and later president of the National League (1951-69). He worked various jobs in the Reds' public relations department as a teenager.

Bill Giles went on to advance his career in Houston , serving as traveling secretary, publicity director and promotions director for the expansion Colt 45s (later the Astros ) before joining the Phillies following the 1969 season.

Giles joined the Phillies in 1969 as vice president of business operations, arriving as the team prepared to move from Connie Mack Stadium to Veterans Stadium. He changed the team's uniforms in 1970, became executive vice president in 1972, and was part of an ownership group that purchased the team from the Carpenter family in 1981.

Under Giles, the franchise won its first World Series in 1980, the highlight of an eight-year stretch in which the Phillies won the National League East six times.

When the Carpenters put the Phillies up for sale in the spring of 1981, Giles organized a limited partnership to purchase the club on October 29, 1981. He served as team president until 1997, then became chairman. He was named chairman emeritus in 2015.

More than the team's on-field success, Giles became known in Philadelphia for emphasizing entertainment and promotion as part of the baseball experience. He was involved in bringing broadcaster Harry Kalas to the team and helped introduce the Phillie Phanatic mascot, which debuted in 1978.

Giles also served in Major League Baseball leadership, including as honorary National League president. He participated in committees that considered interleague play, expansion and the wild-card postseason format. In 2010, he received the Bud Selig Executive Leadership Award for lifetime achievement.

Giles was preceded in death by his wife, Nancy, and is survived by his three sons, Michael, Joseph and Christopher, and eight grandchildren.

articles.summary: Pitching wins championships.
articles.body:
While that old adage still holds true, it has taken on a slightly different meaning in today's game, as teams need to successfully utilize their entire pitching staff to make a deep playoff run, rather than simply leaning on two or three starting pitchers to shoulder the load.

Still, a strong performance from the starting staff can give a team a major leg up. The Los Angeles Dodgers were the perfect example of that last October.

Ahead, we've ranked the projected playoff rotations of every postseason contender, focusing on the 13 teams still in the playoff race as the regular season winds down.

The Astros have used 19 different starting pitchers this year while navigating a long list of injuries. The fact that reliever AJ Blubaugh ranks third on the team with 95.1 innings pitched speaks volumes.

Ace Hunter Brown was slowed by a shoulder strain in the first half of the season, but he has returned to form with a 3.11 ERA and 81 strikeouts in 66.2 innings since the All-Star break.

With Cristian Javier making an early exit from his start on Wednesday, the rotation behind Brown is entirely up in the air. Hayden Wesneski and Peter Lambert are both capable of tossing a quality start, but they are short on big-game experience and could also be susceptible to a quick hook, shifting the focus to a Houston bullpen that ranks 17th in the majors with a 4.09 ERA.

The White Sox rank 26th in starters' ERA (4.62) and 28th in quality starts (34), so the starting rotation is something they will need to figure out how to navigate in the postseason rather than a strength.

Sean Burke and Davis Martin have accounted for 21 of those 33 quality starts. They will be asked to chew up innings at the top of the rotation, while games outside of their starts will likely be an all-hands-on-deck situation.

Sean Newcomb (58 G, 6 GS, 3.17 ERA, 88.0 IP) and Grant Taylor (59 G, 4 GS, 2.30 ERA, 82.0 IP) are both capable of providing length out of the bullpen, while deadline pickup Luis Castillo has also been shifted to a relief role.

Other Candidates: RHP Clay Holmes, RHP Javier Assad

articles.title: Worst records to make MLB playoffs: How Astros, Rangers could clinch with losing record
articles.summary: Here's the history that the Astros and Rangers are facing this week.
articles.body:
As the MLB playoffs approach, the AL West is guaranteed to have one of the worst division winners in league history.

The Houston Astros and Texas Rangers are fighting for the top of the division but are both at risk of doing so with a losing record. While other leagues have produced playoff teams with losing records, MLB has never had many issues with losing teams in the postseason.

Due to the MLB playoff system that guarantees playoff spots to division winners, the Astros and Rangers just have to worry about beating each other out. However, the weaker American League in 2026 makes it so that the AL West winner will also be one of the six best teams in the league.

Here's the history that the Astros and Rangers are facing this week.

Has a team with a losing record ever made the MLB playoffs?

No team with a losing record has ever made the MLB playoffs, but a few have come close. The 2005 Padres made the playoffs at 82-80, putting them just one loss away from a .500 record and two losses away from a losing record.

That Padres team won five of its final six games to finish the year just barely above-.500, but San Diego was still five-games better than the second place Diamondbacks in the NL West. However, the Padres ran into the buzzsaw Cardinals in the NLDS, with St. Louis winning 100 games on the year for the most in the majors that season.

This year, however, either the Astros or Rangers will surpass the 2005 Padres. Both Texas and Houston have 81 losses, guaranteeing that neither will have a winning record on the year, but one of the two will still end up in the playoffs.

Of all the teams to ever win the World Series, the 2006 Cardinals did so with the worst record. St. Louis had a record of 83-78 but won the NL Central, then beat the Padres in the NLDS, Mets in the NLCS and the Tigers in the World Series.

Only once has a team made the playoffs while losing 80 games, as the 2005 Padres hold the record for worst record to ever make the MLB playoffs. San Diego was just two game over .500 when the team won the NL West in 2005, but the Padres were swept by the Cardinals in the NLDS.

Of the next six teams on the list, three were in the last three years thanks to the expanded wild card in both leagues. The 2025 Reds clinched the final wild card spot at 83-79, while the 2023 Marlins and Diamondbacks both made the playoffs with records of 84-78.

However, the team with the worst record to win the World Series is the 2006 Cardinals, who won the NL Central at 83-78 before taking home the title. Due to the division title, that St. Louis team made the playoffs despite not having a top-four record in the National League, while there were eight AL teams that produced better records than the eventual World Series champions.

articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Max Scherzer says he hasn't yet decided whether his Saturday start against the visiting Cincinnati Reds will be the final appearance of his MLB career.

"The only thing I'll say about my future here is I'm going to make this decision about playing next year later in the offseason," Schertzer told reporters Saturday.

Justin Verlander honored before final MLB start

Scherzer is expected to start Sunday's matchup against the Reds, which will mark the Blue Jays' last game of the season following the club's elimination from playoff contention.

He said Saturday he'd been eyeing the game "for a couple weeks" with the goal of pitching again in front of his children, who couldn't make it to Baltimore for his most recent start Wednesday at the Orioles.

"Just want to go out there and pitch tomorrow knowing that, hey, you never know, it could be my last," Scherzer said.

This marks the 18th start of the season for Scherzer, who turned 42 in July and spent significant stretches of this campaign on the injured list.

He is heading into Saturday with a career-high 6.14 ERA and 1.365 WHIP through 77.2 innings pitched.

Schertzer dealt with thumb issues throughout his first season in Toronto before re-signing with the Jays on a one-year, $3 million deal this offseason.

He missed time during his second campaign in Toronto with health issues including right forearm tendinitis, left ankle inflammation and back spasms.

Scherzer told reporters Saturday he feels healthier heading into the offseason, but named the upcoming expiration of MLB's labor agreement as a reason to remain uncertain about his plans for 2027.

"I've gone through ups and downs through this season, I get it, but I've gotten to this point where I'm pretty healthy," Scherzer said. "I've talked to everybody in my inner circle, and we all kind of feel the same way: We don't need to make a decision today. Get to the offseason, and just see how things unfold."

Sunday's start will cap off a 19-year MLB career during which Scherzer won three Cy Young Awards with the Washington Nationals to go along with World Series titles with the Nationals and Texas Rangers.

Scherzer's health, how the Blue Jays react to their stymied World Series hopes, and the status of ongoing CBA negotiations could all impact what the pitcher's future looks like as he prepares to hit unrestricted free agency ahead of his age-43 season.

Verlander also retires with 266 career wins, which is tied for 37th on Major League Baseball's all-time list, plus 3,560 strikeouts, which are the eighth-most in MLB history.

The Detroit Tigers and their fans celebrated the career of longtime ace Justin Verlander on Friday night with a pregame ceremony and his daughter throwing out the ceremonial first pitch.

On Saturday, the former American League MVP, three-time Cy Young Award winner and Rookie of the Year took the mound for the final time for a fanbase at Detroit's Comerica Park that cheered him on for 14 seasons.

Verlander, 43, walked out to the mound by himself without his teammates taking their positions on the field, allowing the fans an opportunity to show their appreciation for the ace who helped the Tigers to one of the most successful runs in franchise history.

He began by retiring the Pittsburgh Pirates (managed by former teammate Don Kelly ) in order in the first inning. Then he shared a moment with home plate umpire Laz Diaz, who is also working his final major-league game. Diaz did the standard check for illegal substances and exchanged pleasantries with Verlander, who patted him on the shoulder.

Verlander's final start ended after getting Brandon Lowe to pop out in foul territory to begin the sixth inning.

Tigers manager A.J. Hinch left the dugout to take him out and Verlander's daughter ran out to the mound to give her father a hug. Verlander left the mound to a standing ovation from the sell-out crowd and his teammates standing outside the dugout.

Verlander finished with 5 1/3 innings, allowing home runs to Lowe and Jacob Gonzalez among 5 hits. He struck out six batters, with Ronny Simon being the final one of his 3,560 strikeouts. (Verlander's first career strikeout was Cleveland's Travis Hafner in 2005.)

Though he didn't get the decision, the Tigers gave Verlander an ending to remember, with Eduardo Valencia walking it off with a two-run homer in the bottom of the ninth for a 4-3 win . That provided another happy memory amid a disappointing season. (Detroit is 76-85 after making the postseason during the previous two years.)

Injuries prevented Verlander from MLB farewell tour

The veteran right-hander last pitched at Comerica Park in a Tigers uniform on Aug. 20, 2017 , when he held the Los Angeles Dodgers to one run with nine strikeouts over eight innings. He was traded to the Houston Astros nearly two weeks later .

S igning a one-year deal with the team that originally drafted him ( No. 2 overall in 2004 ) and for whom he played the majority of his 21-year MLB career, he was hoping to have a celebratory goodbye season with the Tigers.

However, left hip inflammation and a strained left hamstring limited him to only one appearance this year and prevented Verlander from having much of a farewell tour. Before Saturday, he had only pitched once this season, starting a 9-6 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks on March 30. With five runs and six allowed over 3 2/3 innings and only one strikeout, it wasn't an outing to remember.

Verlander was originally set to pitch in Detroit on June 21 (Father's Day), but his hamstring injury prevented that . Just over two weeks later, he announced that he would retire at the end of the 2026 season . He was subsequently named to the AL All-Star team as a "Legend Pick" by MLB commissioner Rob Manfred.

The next time Verlander is seen in a public, baseball-related capacity may be when he's elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame. During his 21 seasons, Verlander compiled a record of 266-159, finishing among the top 10 career leaders in strikeouts . (He currently ranks eighth, but former teammate Max Scherzer will likely move past him on the all-time list.)

He won two World Series championships with the Astros, pitched three no-hitters, was named to 10 All-Star teams. Additionally, Verlander led the AL in ERA twice, wins four times and strikeouts five times.

Verlander wasn't the only one pitching his final MLB game

Also making the final pitching appearance of his MLB career was Kirby Yates , who started Saturday's game for the Pirates as the opener. That was the first start for the career reliever, who pitched 12 big-league seasons.

Yates went 1 2/3 innings, allowing no runs and two hits before being relieved by Yohan Ramírez and receiving congratulations from his teammates and coaches. He ends his career with a 3.35 ERA, 101 saves and 672 strikeouts in 495 innings.

articles.title: 'I Was Sobbing,' Justin Verlander Talks Mound Visit From Daughter in Video After Final MLB Start
articles.summary: Justin Verlander discussed his emotional reaction to his daughter, Genevieve, joining him on the mound as he exited his final MLB start on Saturday.
articles.body:
Justin Verlander discussed his emotional reaction to his daughter, Genevieve, joining him on the mound as he exited his final MLB start on Saturday.

"The way it went with Genevieve running out, I had no clue," Verlander told reporters after the game (0:33 mark). "Totally blindsided. It hit me like a ton of bricks, that was amazing. I was sobbing and had to tell her just to make sure that she understood I was happy. She was fine, I just wanted to make sure she was fine. She hasn't seen me cry like that."

"Walking off the field with my family, obviously we've talked a lot about how my life has changed and what my family means to me and what I'm looking forward to most in retirement, to be able to walk off the field with them, I can't think of a better ending," he added.

Justin Verlander honored before final MLB start

Verlander pitched five innings in the Detroit Tigers' 4-3 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Saturday before he was removed with one out in the top of the sixth.

As Tigers manager A.J. Hinch exited the dugout to take out the right-hander, Verlander's daughter also entered the field to meet her father as his legendary MLB career came to a close.

Verlander was later congratulated by his teammates as well as the rest of his family.

It wasn't the only time that his seven-year-old daughter was involved in his retirement festivities, as she previously threw the ceremonial first pitch to her father ahead of Detroit's 8-7 victory over Pittsburgh on Friday.

"It's been awesome. We've been practicing," Verlander said beforehand, per MLB.com's Jason Beck . "She's all pumped up about it. We actually came out here to the field and practiced off the mound one day. I asked her, 'Where do you want to go? You want to go to the mound?' And she's like, 'The mound.' I'm like, 'That's my girl.'

"She's been really excited. At home, she wants to grab a baseball and go up to play catch with me, which is the first time this has happened. I don't push on her at all, so to have her want to go play catch in the backyard has been awesome, and she's glowing about it."

Verlander announced his plan to retire at the end of the 2026 season in July.

On Saturday, the 43-year-old officially wrapped up a stellar career in which he tallied 10 All-Star nods, three Cy Young Awards, two World Series titles and one American League MVP award.

Verlander will step away from the sport with a 3.33 ERA, while his 3,560 strikeouts rank No. 8 on the all-time MLB leaderboard.

articles.title: The Rays have the best record in the AL. They're about to pay for it
articles.summary: Only one of the AL's top three teams by record will make the ALCS.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays have been the most successful team in the American League this season. Years of good decisions and wins on the margins have yielded a 97-63 record going into the final weekend of the season. They have little left to play for, with enough cushion to guarantee home-field advantage through the ALCS.

In most sports, that position would mean an advantageous path in the playoff bracket. But not MLB.

Instead, the Rays will be rewarded with either the team with the second-best record in the AL or the third-best, via a quirk in MLB's playoff structure. Tampa Bay is guaranteed to face the winner of the wild-card series of the 93-68 New York Yankees or the 87-74 Boston Red Sox , the only teams in the AL with a better run differential than it entering Saturday.

The other side of the AL bracket will be a combination of the 84-76 Cleveland Guardians , the 83-77 Chicago White Sox , the 79-81 Houston Astros or the 79-81 Texas Rangers .

In summary, only one of the AL's top 3 teams can make the ALCS, including its two most popular teams in the Yankees and Red Sox.

The situation is a byproduct of MLB's desire to make division titles matter. Every division champion receives either a first-round bye or a home series against the worst wild-card team available.

It makes sense, in seasons where all of the division champions are at least good teams. That descriptions applies to most years, but not 2026. The Astros and Rangers are still fighting things out in the AL West, but the winner is guaranteed to become the first division winner without a winning record in MLB history .

So what is MLB to do? Does it follow the example of the NBA, where teams are seeded regardless of division? The NHL, where its four divisions matter even more? Or perhaps the NFL, which also has first-round byes and will also give a division champ a home game against a wild-card team with a better record.

In the NFL's case, the league reseeds teams after the wild-card round, which is something else MLB could do. Imagine a world in which the Astros/Rangers get their wild-card series against the White Sox, but then become the lowest seed and face the Rays in the ALDS.

The answer might also be to do nothing and accept that this year's AL West is a once-in-a-generation train wreck.

Either way, it's all very awkward. None of this is to say the Rays have an unreasonable task in front of them. Both the Yankees and Red Sox have significant injury issues, most notably Aaron Judge's calf strain . It's just that brackets are supposed to make at least a little sense when records are included next to the teams.

articles.title: Justin Verlander fights back tears as Kate Upton joins him for emotional farewell before final MLB start
articles.summary: Justin Verlander fought back tears as he stood on the field at Comerica Park with wife Kate Upton and their children during an emotional ceremony Friday.
articles.body: Justin Verlander fought back tears as he stood on the field at Comerica Park with wife Kate Upton and their children during an emotional ceremony Friday. Verlander is set to make the final start of his MLB career on Saturday, ending a 21-year run in baseball. His daughter, Genevieve, threw the ceremonial first pitch before running into her father’s arms. Upton watched from the field with their 1-year-old son, Bellamy, as Verlander thanked Detroit fans and spoke about leaving baseball to spend more time with his family.Justin Verlander gets emotional as Kate Upton and children join farewellVerlander told the Comerica Park crowd, “I am, and always will be, a Detroit Tiger,” as he struggled to hold back tears. His daughter Genevieve then threw out the first pitch and ran into his arms, making it a deeply personal moment. The children wore Tigers jackets with their father’s name and No. 35.Verlander, who began his MLB career with Detroit in 2005, returned to the Tigers this year for his final season after playing for the Houston Astros. MLB says he enters his last start with 266 wins and 3,554 strikeouts. He has won three Cy Young Awards and two World Series titles.Friday, Verlander explained why he decided to stop playing. “I feel like I ran my race. I gave it everything I had,” he said. He also pointed to his children as a reason. “I see my daughter, who’s seven now, and how fast that goes and how much of that time frame I’ve missed already.“I have a 1-year-old son now. I know that I’m going to be able to be there for him and experience more of that childhood that I missed, unfortunately, with my daughter. Also be there for her in some very formative years coming up.”Justin Verlander opens up on 300 wins, Kate Upton and familyVerlander finished his career with 266 victories, falling short of the 300-win mark that had once looked possible. He admitted that missing the milestone was disappointing, but said it did not leave him feeling that he had failed to give everything to baseball.“I think it’s all how you look at it, right? I could be sad for what maybe I didn’t do. I didn’t make 300 wins. That was a goal.“I’m not going to go home and lay my head on my pillow tomorrow night, no matter how the game goes, and be like, I left something out there. I think that gives me some ease.”Upton and Verlander married in Italy in 2017, after he won the World Series with Houston. They first met during a commercial shoot in 2012 and began dating in 2014.Verlander has also spoken about how Upton supported him during a difficult period in his career. In 2018, he said, “She was instrumental in me not … like, jumping off a bridge,” before adding that he was depressed and hiding what he was going through.“I was depressed and kind of just upset at the world and trying to hide my own s***.“I don’t like to talk to people about being hurt. As athletes, you’re not supposed to … But [Upton] was someone I could talk to. I mean, basically a therapist. Somebody I could trust with … worries about my career. Worries about, ‘Can I make it?’ Worries about what I’m going through to get back. articles.title: Brewers name Christian Yelich first official team captain in franchise history
articles.summary: Yelich required the approval of Hall of Famer Robin Yount before accepting.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers announced on Saturday that Christian Yelich would be the first official team captain in franchise history.

Team captains are extremely common in the NFL but rare in MLB. Milwaukee has had symbolic captains in the past, including Hall of Famer Robin Yount, but never an official team captain.

Before accepting the title from the organization, Yelich ensured that Yount approved the move to name the outfielder team captain before he agreed to it, according to manager Pat Murphy:

"He had one request: that we ask Robin Yount before we do such a thing. Robin agreed whole-heartedly because in Yeli's mind Robin was the first captain. I think it goes without saying that nothing changes. He's just officially recognized as such."

Yelich has been with the Brewers since the 2018 season. So far with the organization, he has played in 1,089 games, the 13th-most in franchise history. The 34-year-old earned the National League MVP Award in his first season in Milwaukee. He has been a three-time All-Star and has 186 home runs and 616 RBI in his tenure with the Brewers.

The Milwaukee outfielder is currently playing under a seven-year, $188.5 million extension that has him under contract through the 2028 season. There is then a mutual option for the Brewers and Yelich for 2029.

Milwaukee has already clinched not only a playoff berth, but the NL Central title. The Brewers head into Saturday's game with the most wins in MLB (101) and are the only team with more than 100 wins this season.

The Brew Crew is expected to be the No. 1 seed in the National League's playoff bracket and will head into the postseason with Yelich featuring a brand-new "C" on his uniform.

articles.title: Detroit Tigers’ Verlander leaves final start of his career as 7-year-old daughter runs out for a hug
articles.summary: DETROIT — Justin Verlander had just retired the leadoff batter in the sixth inning of his major league finale when Detroit Tigers manager A.J.
articles.body: DETROIT — Justin Verlander had just retired the leadoff batter in the sixth inning of his major league finale when Detroit Tigers manager A.J. Hinch walked from the dugout toward home plate. The pitcher’s 7-year-old daughter suddenly sprinted to the mound. “That completely blindsided me, and it hit me like a ton of bricks,” Verlander said. A stellar career for the 43-year-old right-hander ended with a 4-3, come-from-behind win against the Pittsburgh Pirates on Saturday. Verlander’s emotions will be remembered far more than the score on a meaningless game on the next-to-last day of his 21st big league season. “That was amazing. I was sobbing and had to make sure that she understood I was happy,” Verlander said. “She’s never seen me cry like that.” Genevieve Verlander, wearing a Tigers jersey with her dad’s name and No. 35, saw her cue from Hinch and ran. When she reached the mound she hugged her father, who reached down to embrace her and started shaking. Hinch joined them about 25 seconds later for another hug, and then Verlander was surrounded by Tigers teammates who came to the mound. Hinch had planned Genevieve’s mound trip with Verlander’s wife, model Kate Upton, “It’s hard to surprise a guy who has everything planned and mapped out more than any human I’ve ever been around,” said Hinch, who managed Verlander to the 2017 World Series title with Houston. “We wanted to come up with something special, and his family means everything to him.” A 10-time All-Star and three-time Cy Young Award winner, Verlander left the field from his final mound appearance grasping his daughter’s hand as the Comerica Park crowd gave him a standing ovation. Upton, holding 1-year-old son Bellamy, joined Justin and Genevieve for a group hug on the warning track in front of the Tigers dugout, and Justin high-fived teammates and doffed his cap to the crowd before descending the dugout steps with his family. “I’ve obviously talked a lot about how my life has changed and how my family is what I’m looking forward to most in my retirement,” the pitcher said. “Walking off the field with them to end my career is as good as I could have dreamed.” Hinch brought Miguel Cabrera’s family onto the field when he came out of his final game in 2023. “They don’t normally let non-uniformed people onto the field,” Hinch said. “But they make exceptions for guys who are going to be first-ballot Hall of Famers.” In all, there was a 5½-minute wait until reliever Tyler Kinley threw his first pitch. Verlander allowed two runs and five hits in 5 1/3 innings with one walk and six strikeouts in his 91-pitch outing. He was making his second start of the year and first since March 30 in a season derailed by a sore hip and hamstring injury. “He didn’t want a cameo. He wanted today to be a competitive outing, and we could tell in the third and fourth innings that he wasn’t laboring,” Hinch said. “He certainly left us with a reminder of why he’s one of the best of all time.” Eduardo Valencia’s game-ending homer in Detroit’s 4-3 meant Verlander didn’t take a loss in his finale. He ended 266-159 with a 3.33 ERA and 3,560 strikeouts, eighth on the career list. “That was a great finish to a great day,” Hinch said. “There was no way Justin Verlander was going to take the loss in his last game as a Tiger.” Pittsburgh’s fifth batter, 20-year-old shortstop Konnor Griffin, had not been born when Verlander made his debut for the Tigers on July 4, 2005. Verlander received a standing ovation when he headed to the bullpen to warm up and a longer one when he returned to the dugout before the first pitch. Academy Award winning actor J.K. Simmons, a longtime Tigers fan, announced him as part of Detroit’s starting lineup. Verlander took the field for the first inning to another ovation. He was alone on the field as his teammates stayed in the dugout to give him the spotlight. “That blindsided me, too,” he said. “I probably should have expected it, but I was trying to stick with my routine, so I ran out onto the field. I was ready to go before I realized everyone else was still in the dugout.” Pittsburgh took a 2-0 lead against Verlander on solo homers by Lowe in the fourth and Nick Gonzales in the fifth, the first on a 89.7 mph fastball and the second on a curve. Verlander pitched for the Tigers from 2005-17, then returned this year after time with Houston, the New York Mets and San Francisco. “All the ovations today brought back a lot of fond memories of the old days here, when this park was raucous every night,” Verlander said. “My body, though, didn’t remind me of those days at all.”

articles.title: Phillies enter final day of MLB regular season on verge of unfathomable choke in playoff race
articles.summary: The Phillies could have clinched a playoff spot as soon as Wednesday. Almost nothing has gone right for them since then.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies might really be doing this. We don't mean that in a good way.

As MLB enters the final day of the regular season on Sunday, there is a single National League playoff spot up for grabs. In one corner is the 87-74 Phillies. In the other is the 86-75 Arizona Diamondbacks . The Phillies lead the D-backs by a single game, but Arizona has the tiebreaker.

That leaves a scenario where the Phillies clinch with either a win over the Tampa Bay Rays or a D-backs loss to the San Diego Padres . It's a narrow path to victory for Arizona, but it's an astonishing turn of events the club is alive at all.

With the divisions all but decided, the Phillies were tied with both the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres in the wild-card race at 87-70 with five games to play. The D-backs were dead in the water, trailing the trio by four games. Arizona could have been eliminated from playoff contention as early as Wednesday.

Here is how every game has gone since then for the D-backs:

And here is what the Phillies have done:

In summary, the Phillies have spent four straight days exactly one good day from clinching a playoff spot, which the Padres and Cubs both did Thursday. They have been outscored 23-3 in those four days.

To be fair, the Phillies have faced the No. 1 seeds in the NL (Brewers) and AL (Rays) in that span. Those are tough matchups, but that's also kind of the point of making the playoffs. The Phillies have needed only two of 10 games to go their way to clinch a playoff spot, and only one has, the Padres' win on Saturday.

Philadelphia has looked more listless with every game, right up to its blowout loss at the hands of Tampa . That was a game in which the Phillies maneuvered their rotation to start Aaron Nola on two days' rest, when they would want to be saving him for the playoffs. He pitched a single inning, allowing four hits and three runs.

The club will break even more glass due to emergency on Sunday, with Zack Wheeler taking the mound and Jesús Luzardo getting activated to be available out of the bullpen . That is full elimination-game mode, two days before a hypothetical playoff berth would begin.

Whomever gets the final wild card will face the Atlanta Braves in a best-of-three series starting Tuesday.

Even if Sunday goes the Phillies' way, they are still facing an ominous situation in a season that was supposed to be one of their best remaining chances with their current core. They rank fourth in MLB in payroll at $289 million for 2026 and are coming off back-to-back division titles with one of the oldest rosters in MLB.

Bryce Harper is in his age 33 season. Same with Kyle Schwarber and Trea Turner . Wheeler is 36. Cristopher Sánchez is 29. Nola is 33. That's not a group anyone can expect to get better with time, only worse, and there aren't many reasons for optimism coming from the minor-league ranks, not when the Philadelphia farm system was ranked only the 26th best in baseball by MLB Pipeline last month .

It's the kind of situation that leads to an uncomfortable offseason any time the team fails to win a World Series. Depending on how Sunday goes, Philadelphia could be in for several more degrees of uncomfortable this winter.

articles.title: MLB's 8 Biggest Winners and Losers of 2026 Regular Season
articles.summary: Sunday is the final day of the 2026 MLB season, which means before the postseason begins, it's time for some reflection on the last six months.
articles.body:
Sunday is the final day of the 2026 MLB season, which means before the postseason begins, it's time for some reflection on the last six months.

2026 will likely feature first-time winners for NL and AL MVP, along with NL and AL Cy Young. Still, there were plenty of usual suspects who had excellent seasons as well.

Before we turn the page on the 2026 regular season, here's a look at the eight biggest winners and losers of the campaign.

There was no question entering the season whether Pete Crow-Armstrong was one of the best defenders in baseball. However, he posted just a .634 OPS after the All-Star Game a year ago, leading to questions about just how good he was offensively, particularly when he wasn't hitting the ball out of the park.

Well, Crow-Armstrong has answered those questions by hitting 45 homers, driving in 107 runs and posting a .941 OPS in 2026. Add in his 41 stolen bases and 119 runs scored, and he's been one of the best offensive players in baseball in 2026. When you consider his continued greatness in center field, it's not surprising that he leads all hitters with a 10.7 WAR. According to FanGraphs , the next closest player in terms of WAR is Bobby Witt Jr., who is at 6.9.

Not only will PCA win his second Gold Glove, but he'll have a case for the Platinum Glove as the best defender in the National League. And, 10 years after Kris Bryant won NL MVP for the Cubs, Crow-Armstrong is going to dethrone Shohei Ohtani and win the honor.

Jacob Misiorowski was arguably the biggest story of the 2026 season, as he turned in one of the most dominant campaigns in modern history. He did so while averaging over 100 mph on his fastball, something we haven't really ever seen from a starter over a full season.

In many years, this would have been an incredible NL Cy Young Award race considering how well Cristopher Sánchez, Chris Sale, Jesús Luzardo and Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched. In this year, though, the Cy Young race was pretty much over by August.

Misiorowski will ultimately finish the season as the MLB leader in ERA, ERA+, FIP, WHIP, K/9 and WAR, per FanGraphs . It's hard to be much more dominant than that.

Even if he had to settle for runner-up in AL MVP voting to Aaron Judge in 2025, Cal Raleigh put together arguably the greatest season we've ever seen from a catcher, as he launched 60 home runs and drove in 125 runs.

"The Big Dumper" definitely had a hangover in 2026, hitting .169 with just nine home runs and a .581 OPS in the first half. By just about any metric, he was one of the worst everyday players in baseball.

He's rebounded to some degree since the All-Star Break, as he has a .761 OPS since the Midsummer Classic. Still, Raleigh checked in at No. 8 on B/R's countdown of the top 25 players in baseball entering the season. He won't even really be in consideration for it in 2027 based on how he performed for most of 2026.

Yankees vs. Red Sox AL Wild Card Preview 🔮

If for nothing more than the Mets having a top-five payroll and missing the playoffs for the second consecutive season, New York president of baseball operations David Stearns is one of the biggest losers of the 2026 MLB season.

Following a second-half collapse, Stearns drastically remade the roster in his image. The early results weren't promising:

Stearns traded Brandon Nimmo to the Texas Rangers for Marcus Semien . Granted, part of the calculation here was that Nimmo is signed through 2030, while Semien's deal is up after 2028. But at 36 years old, Semien seems to have almost nothing left offensively. Nimmo wasn't great, either, but still has a 112 OPS+, as opposed to 74 from Semien.

The Mets let closer Edwin Díaz walk in free agency, and judging off of the results of his first season on a three-year, $60.03 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers, that might have been wise choice. The problem is Stearns gave Devin Williams a three-year, $41.38 million pact to be New York's closer, only for him to post a 4.54 ERA across 43 appearances in his first year in Flushing.

The worst one of them all was letting Pete Alonso leave for a five-year, $155 million contract with the Baltimore Orioles. While Alonso topped 40 homers for the fourth time in his career, his replacement, Jorge Polanco , hit .148 in just 37 games.

The Mets did play better after the All-Star Break, earning interim manager Andy Green the job on a full-time basis. Owner Steve Cohen has stood by Stearns, who did put together a team that reached the NLCS just two years ago. However, the addition of former Minnesota Twins president of baseball operations Derek Falvey to the front office as a senior advisor is a sign that Cohen is growing impatient.

Cam Schlittler emerged on the national scene in Game 3 of the ALWCS a year ago, when he struck out 12 Boston Red Sox over eight shutout innings in an elimination game.

He proved to have staying power this year, a season he'll end as the junior circuit's leader in WAR, ERA, ERA+ and WHIP. Dylan Cease gave him a good run for his money, but Schlittler is going to win the AL Cy Young Award.

Based off of what he did in his first career postseason appearance a year ago, Schlittler's magical 2026 might still have another chapter in store as the Yankees try to emerge from a wide-open AL playoff field.

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. didn't have a great week in the public relations department:

But the truth is, Guerrero would have been on this list even before the comments.

Last October, Guerrero looked like the best hitter in the planet, batting .397 with eight home runs and a 1.289 OPS for a Blue Jays team that made it to Game 7 of the World Series. This year, the Blue Jays will be at home in October. There's plenty of blame to go around for that, but Guerrero not hitting a home run at home until mid-September certainly didn't help.

In the end, Guerrero is still going to play next season at 28, so he's still young. There's no reason to think he isn't a great face for their franchise. But the first season of a 14-year, $500 million deal didn't go as planned.

Yordan Alvarez was limited to just 48 games in 2025 because of a right hand fracture and left ankle sprain. Still, we snuck him on our B/R list of the top 25 MLB players entering the 2026 season on a hunch.

As it turns out, we didn't listen to that hunch enough. Alvarez was No. 20 coming into 2026. He'll probably be in the top five in 2027 after nearly winning the AL Triple Crown in 2026. Alvarez is likely to join Jeff Bagwell and José Altuve as the only players in Astros history to win MVPs.

If you add an MVP to Alvarez's resume—which includes AL Rookie of the Year, four All-Star selections, ALCS MVP and what was essentially a World Series winning homer in 2022—you can start to see a pretty compelling Hall of Fame case coming together for the 29-year-old.

Remember when there were people suggesting that the 2026 season wasn't even worth playing because Kyle Tucker signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers made them a shoo-in to win their third consecutive World Series?

Well, the Dodgers could still three-peat, but it hasn't been a very impressive first season in Los Angeles for Tucker. After signing a four-year, $240 million contract that includes a player opt out after the second season, Tucker has produced just a 98 OPS+ in 2026. Mind you, 100 is considered a league average player, and Tucker averaged a 142 OPS+ from 2020-2025.

Tucker is finishing the season on a high note, as he has a .921 OPS in September. If he has a big October, no one will remember how much he struggled during the regular season. But this has definitely been an underwhelming campaign for the four-time All-Star.

articles.title: Top MLB Free Agents Rumors Before 2026 Regular-Season Ends
articles.summary: As the MLB Playoffs approach, eliminated teams are already focusing on free agency.
articles.body:
As the MLB Playoffs approach, eliminated teams are already focusing on free agency.

Several top players, including Tarik Skubal and Sonny Gray, are preparing to enter the market.

Below, we'll do our best to predict landing spots by analyzing rumors and identifying top fits.

It's no secret the Yankees need a new second baseman.

Jazz Chisholm Jr., set to enter free agency as an unrestricted free agent, has struggled to get his bat going all year.

There are a number of talented second basemen set to hit the market.

In Pittsburgh, Brandon Lowe is having one of his best seasons, with 34 home runs and 95 RBIs.

Meanwhile, in Philadelphia, Luis Arraez has played well despite questions about his defense.

Lowe may be in the midst of a career year, but Arraez has been one of the league's best hitters for several seasons now.

It seems likely the Yankees would target him, since Jon Heyman reported they already showed interest in him at the trade deadline.

With positional fit no longer an issue, bringing in Arraez could revamp a Yankees lineup that currently ranks in the bottom five in batting average.

Did anyone see this coming from Sonny Gray at 36 years old?

The right-hander is tied for the most wins (18) in MLB this season and owns the eighth-best ERA (2.72) in the league.

Gray is arguably having the best season of his career. Plus, with the Red Sox sending Connelly Early to the Nationals at the deadline, they'll need to hold on to their starting pitching.

According to Mass Live's Chris Cotillo , Gray could be looking at a contract in the three-year, $75 million range. There's just one slight concern: as Gray told The Boston Globe , he would retire "in a heartbeat" if that's what his family wanted.

After a career-best year, though, retirement seems unlikely, with a reunion seemingly making sense for both sides.

No matter how you look at it, this offseason feels like it all revolves around Skubal landing a monster record-breaking deal.

Jeff Passan summed it up: the numbers for Skubal's next contract will be massive. He's about to turn 30, and there's really no precedent for the kind of payday he could command. With teams willing to spend big and no salary cap holding anyone back, the bidding could get wild.

Skubal's track record speaks for itself. Sure, he's dealt with some injuries this season, but he still resembles the two-time reigning AL Cy Young winner he is.

Given the high price tag, only a few teams will have a chance. The Mets are always looking to make a splash; the Padres and Yankees might throw their hats in the ring.

But one thing is certain: letting Skubal walk seems almost unthinkable for the Dodgers.

Chaos is the only word needed to describe the final day of the 2026 MLB regular season.

The Phillies held a 6.5-game lead for the third Wild Card spot on September 1st. They still lead the Diamondbacks by one game, but Arizona controls the tie-breaker. The Phillies can avoid a full-on collapse with either a win or a Diamondbacks loss.

With the Padres' win on Saturday, they locked up the top wild card spot and will host the Cubs in a rematch of last year's wild card matchup.

Meanwhile, in the AL West, the Astros and Rangers are tied at the top, with the Astros holding the tiebreaker. The winner of the division will make history as the first team to claim a division title with a non-winning record in a 162-game season.

On Saturday, the Cleveland Guardians secured the 2-seed with a win and Chicago White Sox loss.

This leaves the only playoff drama for Sunday in the AL West, where the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers are tied for the division lead.

Whoever wins the division will make history as the first team to claim a division title without a winning record in a 162-game season.

The Astros have the tiebreaker, so if they beat the Athletics, they'll clinch the third seed. The Athletics are turning to a bullpen game, starting Brady Basso. The Astros have everything on the line, and with Oakland's league-worst bullpen, Houston looks poised to lock up a playoff spot.

The Philadelphia Phillies should be sending a thank-you note to the San Diego Padres.

After all, San Diego is the only reason the Phillies still control their postseason fate. The Padres won against the Diamondbacks on Saturday, locking up the top wild card spot and setting up a rematch with the Chicago Cubs.

For Philly fans, the Padres win ensured that the team would wake up Sunday still one game ahead of the Diamondbacks for the third Wild Card spot.

But the Diamondbacks own the tie-breaker and, with a win and a Phillies loss, will leapfrog Philadelphia and cement one of the most epic collapses in recent times.

The Phillies have lost four straight, scoring just three runs total.

The bats have to get going eventually, and with a resurgent Zack Wheeler on the mound behind the home crowd, I expect them to beat the Tampa Bay Rays and punch their postseason ticket.
